messages:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: PAGED: P1 - latency SLO breach & 502 spike for hosted runtime (us-west1). Incident INC-2026-412. Affected: /v1/generate and chat endpoints. Symptoms: sustained queue depth > 1200, pod restarts in gpu-pool-a. Link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-412
ellie: ack - I'm taking pager. grabbing graphs now, will post timeline.
mike: I'm on traces & model routing. noticing many warmup misses (cache miss ratio ~92%).
kevin: I'll check HPA and metrics adapter. running: `kubectl -n runtime get hpa gpu-deploy -o yaml`
infra-bot: HPA gpu-deploy targets: metric: custom.queue_length, target: 50, current: 1200, lastScaleTime: "2026-03-15T02:10:05Z", metrics-server-latency: 46s
ellie: timeline so far - 02:08 UTC queue depth started climbing, 02:09 SLO alerts fire, 02:10 several nginx 502s, 02:11 first pod OOMKilled in gpu-pool-a, 02:12 autoscaler attempted to scale but new pods not accepting traffic (warmup delay).
sara: logs from runtime warmup service (excerpt):
```
[02:10:32] warmup-service: initializing model redwood-alpha-1 on gpu-0
[02:11:05] kv-cache: miss, loading weights from disk
[02:11:32] warmup-service: loaded weights, starting compilation
[02:12:40] warmup-service: compilation timeout after 60s, retrying
[02:13:10] warmup-service: warmup succeeded
```
kevin: prometheus-adapter shows scrape gaps 02:09-02:11 for custom metrics; metrics-server CPU utilization spike. looks like adapter didn't report queue_length for ~90s so HPA didn't see gradual increase until it was huge.
mike: hypothesis: metric reporting delay + high cold-start warmup time => autoscaler scaled but pods remained cold -> extreme queueing and user-facing 502s.
ellie: mitigation actions executed: 1) routed 30% traffic to a smaller model redwood-alpha-1-small (less GPU mem, faster warmup) 2) bumped HPA max replicas to +50% via `kubectl patch` 3) forced warmup by sending synthetic warmup requests to new pods.
kevin: commands used:
```
kubectl -n runtime patch hpa gpu-deploy --type=merge -p '{"spec": {"maxReplicas": 60}}'
for pod in $(kubectl -n runtime get pods -l app=runtime,gpu=true -o name); do curl -sS http://$pod:8080/health || true; done
```
mike: after routing and forced warmup latency dropped by ~60% within 3m. 502 rate reduced to baseline at 02:20 UTC.
sara: customer impact estimate: ~8% of requests saw 502s during 02:09-02:20; top affected customers: small-mid ecommerce workloads that spike token lengths. notified CSMs.
ellie: adding running hypotheses to thread: [H1] metrics-adapter scrape latency & aggregator backlog masked queue metric -> HPA reaction was delayed. [H2] warmup/service compile path has a rare +60s compilation stall when disk I/O/pack load high. [H3] placement/routing skew put too many new pods on same host causing local NVMe contention.
kevin: collecting logs: pushed aggregator logs to /incidents/INC-2026-412/metrics-adapter.log and warmup traces to /incidents/INC-2026-412/warmup-traces.log. sharing sample below:
```
metrics-adapter: 02:09:12 fetchProm: timeout after 30s
metrics-adapter: 02:10:05 reconnected to prometheus cluster
```
ellie: next actions before handoff: - create RCA timeline doc (I'll start doc draft) - short-term: add 15s fallback for HPA (if metric missing, use CPU) and lower warmup compile timeout to 30s in staging - long-term: add direct queue_length scrape path and prioritized warmup queue + pre-warming heuristics.
mike: I'll open PR to add fallback in HPA config and a canary for warmup timeout change. linking PR when ready.
sara: I've started customer comms template and flagged top 5 tenants.
infra-bot: Note: autoscaler event log shows scale up events at 02:12, nodes added at 02:14, pods created 02:15, readiness probes failing until 02:18.
ellie: ok handing off to @kevin for midnight shift follow-up. Kevin - please validate logs for NVMe I/O contention and confirm whether placement rules need change.
kevin: ack handoff. I'll run `iostat` on hosts where pods landed and check kernel dmesg for I/O errors. tagging follow-ups in the RCA doc.
ellie: leaving notes for on-call rotation: runbook checklist executed? yes (forced warmup, routing, HPA bump). add retrospective point: consider allowing automated temporary routing to smaller model variant when warmup backlog detected.
mike: quick note - we should also add a guard in the router that detects sustained queue_depth > 200 and automatically reduce max-req-size to favor throughput.
sara: putting incident in postmortem queue. I'll create postmortem draft and assign owners.
kevin: initial low-confidence root cause: combination of prometheus-adapter scrape gap (metrics blindspot) + long warmup compile under high I/O -> autoscaler reaction + slow pod readiness => queue overflow. Confidence: medium.
ellie: thanks everyone. closing incident page and moving to RCA thread. please add any missing logs or observations here. :thumbsup:
